title: Massachusetts guidance measures a nonresident prescriber's five-day Schedule II validity from the do-not-fill-before date
subtopic: A nonresident prescriber's Schedule II prescriptions and the do-not-fill-before date
rule_summary: The Board of Registration in Pharmacy's December 2025 newsletter, in its item Multiple Schedule II Prescriptions, states that federal law allows prescribers to issue multiple Schedule II prescriptions (up to a 90-day supply) using the date of issuance (date written) and a 'do not fill before' date; that since prescriptions may not be post-dated, the clock would start from the later 'do not fill before' date (if there is one); and that, if issued by a nonresident prescriber, Schedule II prescriptions are only valid for five days from the date of issuance or the 'do not fill before' date, as applicable. The same item gives the Massachusetts prescriber's period as 30 days from the date of issuance or the 'do not fill before' date, as applicable.
exam_relevance: Tests how the five-day period for a nonresident prescriber's Schedule II prescription applies to the later prescriptions of a federal multiple-prescription set: the guidance measures it from the do-not-fill-before date where there is one, so a later prescription does not lapse merely because the set was dated at a visit more than five days earlier.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy newsletter, December 2025, Vol. 9, No. 2

numeric_facts.fact: validity of a nonresident prescriber's Schedule II prescription
numeric_facts.conditions: measured from the do-not-fill-before date where the prescription carries one, and otherwise from the date of issuance

common_confusions: For a nonresident prescriber's Schedule II prescription carrying a do-not-fill-before date, the guidance measures the five days from that date, not from the date written.
The five-day period the guidance gives a nonresident prescriber's Schedule II prescriptions is not the 30-day period it gives a Massachusetts prescriber's.
verification_notes: Read the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's December 2025 newsletter (MA Vol. 9, No. 2) on 2026-09-16: the item Multiple Schedule II Prescriptions on page 1 and the publication statement on page 5, which says the newsletter is published by the Board and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy Foundation to promote compliance of pharmacy and drug law and that its opinions and views do not necessarily reflect the official views, opinions, or policies of the Foundation or the Board unless expressly so stated. The item's closing reminder about accepting Schedule II opioid prescriptions from Maine and contiguous states is not carried by this rule; the out-of-state filling routes in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d) and (d1/2) are carried by MA-OUTSTATE-CII-FILL-WINDOW. Added as a new rule so that no existing record is changed.
